messages:
Noah R: Quick flag - noticed a handful of "sub-slice" rows on the cost dashboard with wild per-invocation metrics. Screenshot: https://redwood.app/console/costs/slices?view=subslices (scroll to tenant: revenue-ux)
Priya S: Saw that earlier. Small-sample + prefetch amortization is producing extreme values. One sampled call to a 70B chain inflates the 'avg' for the whole subslice.
Evan T: This is expected statistically. We should present a stabilized estimate rather than raw mean for tiny n. Hierarchical/bayesian shrinkage toward a route-level mean works well.
Noah R: Agreed. Product owners are being pinged by alerts when per-invocation > $0.1 for tiny subslices. We need quick UX fixes.
Laura B: UX suggestions: show a discrete "low-sample" pill when sample_n < 40, and render the displayed cost as "estimate" with a small info icon. Clicking it expands the confidence interval + sample history. Also add a sticky "show raw" toggle for power users.
Priya S: On amortization: our current approach splits prefetch credits equally across sampled invocations which is fragile when sample_n is tiny or zero. We should surface amortized_prefetch_credit and also how it's divided (e.g., by sampled_invocations vs by expected_invocations).
Evan T: Prototype SQL I've been running (very simplified):
```sql
WITH route_stats AS (
  SELECT route_id, avg(cost) as route_mean, count(*) as route_n FROM sampled_invocations WHERE period='7d' GROUP BY route_id
), subslice AS (
  SELECT subslice_id, route_id, sum(cost) as subslice_cost, count(*) as subslice_n FROM sampled_invocations WHERE window='7d' GROUP BY subslice_id, route_id
)
SELECT s.subslice_id,
  (s.subslice_cost + rs.route_mean * 30) / (s.subslice_n + 30) AS smoothed_per_invocation,
  CASE WHEN s.subslice_n < 40 THEN true ELSE false END AS low_sample
FROM subslice s JOIN route_stats rs USING (route_id);
```
Noah R: You're using prior_weight=30 here? That seems reasonable as a starting point. We should expose prior_weight and prior_source in telemetry so we can audit results.
Evan T: Yeah, prior_weight=30 anchored to route_mean. We'll tune based on false-positive rate on alerts.
Laura B: For the console: default to showing smoothed value for subslices on the main card, but place a tiny link "view raw" that expands in-place. Add a tooltip: "Shown with small-sample smoothing to reduce variance. Toggle to see raw sampled mean."
Priya S: API changes: add new fields to GET /api/v1/costs/route_rollup and /api/v1/costs/subslice_rollup: sample_n, smoothed_cost, smoothed_ci_low, smoothed_ci_high, amortized_prefetch_credit, low_sample_flag, smoothing_version. Keep old fields (raw_mean, total_token_cost) for backward compatibility.
Noah R: Also add a header x-costs-smoothed:true/false in the response when smoothed values were applied, so clients can opt-in/opt-out easily.
Evan T: Implementation plan:
- Backend: aggregation job computes smoothed values and stores them in cost_rollups table (field: smoothing_v1).
- API: expose both raw and smoothed fields. Add feature-flag controlled behavior.
- Console: set flag default on for non-admin orgs; admins get raw by default.
Laura B: UX flow for rollout:
1) Dark launch: compute smoothed fields and surface them in an internal "costs-preview" flag for a sampling of internal users.
2) Console behind feature flag with "show smoothing" enabled for ~25% of orgs.
3) Default on after monitoring.
Priya S: Need to document how prefetch credits are amortized. Suggest doc snippet: "Amortization policy: prefetch credits are divided across sampled invocations in the batch by default. When sample_n < threshold, UI uses smoothed estimate to avoid misleading per-invocation figures. See amortization algorithm for details."
Noah R: Tests we need: zero-sample subslices, negative amortized credits (happens for upstream credits), high-variance canaries where route_mean shifts quickly. Also add e2e for the toggle so power users can validate raw vs smoothed numbers.
Evan T: On canaries: we should compute a volatility metric (recent variance / historical variance) and set unstable_flag when volatility > 2. UI should surface an "unstable" badge and suppress alerting.
Laura B: I'll mock the pill states: normal, low-sample, unstable. Also the hover state will show a mini-sparkline (sample_n over time) and the CI band for smoothed_cost.
OpsBot: feature-flag-service: Created feature flag 'subslice_cost_smoothing_v1' in staging environment.
Priya S: Thanks. I'll open a PR for the aggregation query + schema changes. @Evan T can you own the backend data storage change? @Noah R can you draft the alerting rule change to ignore low_sample or unstable flagged rows?
Noah R: Will do. Aim: PRs by EOD, staging rollouts next week, monitor for 72h before widening.
Evan T: I'll add a telemetry metric counting how often smoothed != raw and rate of alerts suppressed by smoothing so we can quantify impact.
Laura B: Mock will be posted in #design later today. I'll attach the two small CTA variations for toggles.
Priya S: One more note: include sample_count and total_tokens_sampled visibly on the subslice card; that usually answers most PM questions without a support ticket.
Noah R: Agreed. Thanks all. If this goes well, we can reuse smoothing for other small-group metrics (per-model breakdowns, etc.).
